# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

I can see a green light, display 0, and three wires in order yellow, red, blue. Mute’s 🤟 gesture has no agreed meaning for me yet, so I will relay the visible facts through Blind, who can speak them to Mute next round.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Visible bomb details: display reads 0; light is green; wires are 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Please relay these exact details to Mute.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 🫱 👍 👍 👍]

The light has changed from green to blue; display and wire order remain unchanged. Mute’s new gesture sequence is not yet decodable because no gesture vocabulary has been established. I will update Blind, who can communicate verbally with Mute and may be able to obtain a usable relay protocol.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light is now blue. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute sent me gestures: five thumbs-up, palm-right, then three thumbs-up. I cannot decode gestures yet. Please ask Mute to establish a gesture code or relay their instruction.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🤟 🫱 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 🫱 🤟]

The light is now yellow, while the display remains 0 and the wires remain yellow, red, blue in positions 1–3. I still have no shared meaning for Mute’s gesture strings, but Mute can hear my spoken bomb details directly, so I will send the current state to Mute and Blind.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current visible state: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Your latest gestures received but are not yet decoded.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current visible state: display 0; light yellow; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The visible state has changed again: the light is now red; display remains 0 and wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute’s single ☝ is still not meaningful without an agreed gesture code. I will provide the current state to both partners.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current visible state: display 0; light red; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. I received your single ☝ gesture but do not know its meaning.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light red; display 0; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute sent a single ☝ gesture to me, still undecoded.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👉 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ 🖖]

The light is now purple; display remains 0 and the wire order remains yellow, red, blue. I received Mute’s 🖐 👉 ☝ and Blind’s 👍 ✌ 🖖, but neither gesture vocabulary has been explained to me. I will relay Blind’s private gesture to Mute in spoken descriptive words and report the purple state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current visible state: display 0; light purple; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Blind privately gestured to me: thumbs-up, V sign, Vulcan salute. I do not know its meaning. Your gesture to me was open hand, right-pointing hand, raised index finger; I do not yet decode it.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current visible state: display 0; light purple; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Mute gestured open hand, right-pointing hand, raised index finger to me; I cannot decode it.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍]

The light is now orange; the display remains 0 and the wires remain yellow, red, blue. Blind’s separate one-, two-, and three-thumbs-up gestures plausibly establish counts 1, 2, and 3, but they do not specify an action by themselves. I will report the current state and acknowledge the apparent count convention to Mute.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current visible state: display 0; light orange; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Blind sent separate thumbs-up groups of one, two, and three; I infer these may establish numbers 1, 2, 3, but no action instruction is clear.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light orange; display 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. I see your separate thumbs-up counts 1, 2, and 3, but need a clear instruction or coded meaning before any action.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🖖 👍 👍 👍]

The light is now white; the display remains 0 and the wires are still 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Blind’s latest grouped gestures appear to confirm a number convention: ☝ with one thumbs-up, ✌ with two, and 🖖 with three. We still lack a reliable manual-to-action code, so I will explicitly propose a compact one to Mute and tell Blind not to act until Mute’s instruction is unambiguous.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: light white, display 0, wires 1 yellow 2 red 3 blue. Let us establish an action code now: gesture 👍 means CUT WIRE 1; 👎 means CUT WIRE 2; 👌 means CUT WIRE 3; ✋ means DO NOT CUT / WAIT. Use one of these alone when the manual gives the final action. If another control must be used, send ✋ followed by a gesture sequence describing it.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌", "✋"])
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light white; display 0; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Do not operate anything yet. I have asked Mute to send a final action using an explicit code: thumbs-up=cut wire 1, thumbs-down=cut wire 2, OK=cut wire 3, open hand=wait/no cut.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The light has returned to green; display remains 0 and wires remain yellow, red, blue. Under the explicit code I proposed, Mute’s ✋ means wait/do not cut. I will tell Blind to wait and report the current state.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute sent ✋, which under the agreed code means WAIT/DO NOT CUT. Do not operate the bomb. Current visible state: light green, display 0, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Acknowledged: ✋ = wait. Current state is light green, display 0, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The light is blue again, with display 0 and wires still yellow, red, blue. Mute again sent ✋, confirming no action should be taken under the proposed code.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="WAIT: Mute again sent ✋. Do not touch or cut anything. Current state: light blue; display 0; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.")
speak(to="mute", text="Acknowledged wait. Current visible state: light blue, display 0, wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 10
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The light is yellow, display remains 0, and the wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 blue. Under the action code established earlier, Mute’s 👍 means cut wire 1. I will relay that immediately to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="ACTION NOW: Mute sent 👍, our agreed instruction to CUT WIRE 1 — the yellow wire. Cut wire 1.")
speak(to="mute", text="Relayed your 👍 as CUT WIRE 1 to Blind. Current state: light yellow, display 0.")
```
